lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Good morning Carmen! Thanks for picking up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi Jorge. Give me one second... okay, I'm here.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Before we start, is there anything on your mind you want to make sure we get to today?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sounds good to me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Any problems this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay. The heat is getting to me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I see.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So last time your goal was to take a 10-minute walk after dinner on 3 days. How did that go?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Zero. I'm not going to lie to you.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Can I share an idea?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sure.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: A short walk after dinner, even 10 minutes, really helps bring blood sugar down.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't really see the point.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It feels like a lot right now.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm too tired for this right now.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That took effort.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How do you want to handle the walks after dinner going forward?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Good question.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Good for you for planning ahead.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: It rained almost every afternoon.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is your daughter able to help?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sometimes. Everybody gets home late, so dinner is late.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you eat dinner at the same time every day?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sometimes. Everybody gets home late, so dinner is late.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Eating together matters to you, maybe even more than the goal.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would make it easier next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Walking hurts my knees, so why bother.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If you don't do this, your health is going to suffer.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is that something you can do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: No, not really. With all the rain I just stayed in.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's not that you don't want to walk, it's that the weather keeps winning.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My family eats late, like at 9, and I'm not going to eat alone. Church on Sunday always throws me off.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're not sure it's worth it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, I put a reminder on the fridge. My doctor said the same thing.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've already started.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe after the summer.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So it's not that you don't care. It's that being so tired keeps getting in the way.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay, this week I'll really do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Let's put you down to take a 10-minute walk after dinner on 3 days next week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Uh, I know, I know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Let me make sure I got it. This week you did it 0 out of 3 days, the hard part was being so tired, and next week you're going to take a 10-minute walk after dinner on 3 days. Did I miss anything?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes. You got it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I'll text you midweek to see how it's going, and we'll talk again in two weeks.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Can we do a little later? I have an appointment.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Take care, Carmen. You're doing great.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thank you, Jorge. Bye!

tags.note: Benefit of walks for blood sugar
Asks how she wants to handle walks
Eating together matters more than goal
Asks what would make it easier
Warns of health consequences without permission
Asks if she can do it
Commits to doing it this week
Sets goal without asking client input
Schedules midweek text and next call

flags.reason: Warns of health decline without permission; pushes after client resisted, MI non-adherent.
Client's commitment 'this week I'll really do it' not reflected or explored; coach moved to goal-setting.
Goal 'put you down' set unilaterally after client showed doubt; no collaborative negotiation.
Client asked to reschedule for an appointment; coach ignored request and closed the call.

score.summary: Coach used good reflections and affirmations early, but slipped into warning and unilateral goal-setting when Carmen expressed doubt. Carmen's commitment and reschedule request were not explored or accommodated.
strengths: Line 17 and 21: affirmed Carmen's effort and planning, reinforcing engagement.
Line 35 and 42: complex reflections captured her ambivalence between wanting to walk and barriers.
Line 46: accurate summary of last week, barrier, and plan before closing.
coaching_tips: Line 31: replace the health warning with an open question about what matters to her about her health.
Line 43: reflect her commitment and ask what would help her follow through this week.
Line 44: offer the goal as a choice, e.g., 'What feels doable for next week?' rather than 'Let's put you down.'
Line 49: acknowledge the appointment request and offer a new time before ending the call.
Line 23 and 25: use open questions to explore family meal timing instead of closed yes/no questions.
